title: Transition W13: normalize the ADR 0020 bounded capability contract
description:
Workstream W13 of the integrated ADR 0020 transition design (sections 5.4, 5.5,
7.2, and the ADR 0020 section 3 capability contract):
docs/audits/rules-awareness-transition/2026-07-30-integrated-transition-design.md.
That design is the accepted deliverable of eshyra-o9bd.19.8 (PR #485, reviewed
head afd113c7090378c3a9f4122f246a6c32602a5164, merge commit
042ce119aa699f04f60a1885d471335f07745282). ADR 0020 controls. This bead is the
eshyra-olc5 owner of capability-contract shape.

OWNER
This bead owns the normalized shape of a deterministic capability contract under
ADR 0020. No other bead owns it.

SCOPE
Define and apply the positive capability contract. Every capability in force
declares, in band:

1. the operation it performs;
2. its required inputs;
3. its exclusions - what it explicitly does not do;
4. its revision or identity;
5. what interpretation remains with the DM;

and fails closed on unrecognized input.

The first real contract is assertMagicItemOperationReady
(packages/core/src/state/itemExecutionReadiness.ts, revision
derived-magic-item-clauses-v1), which is also the only capability in the
repository carrying an explicit revision identity today. Its unrecognized-scope
fail-open is repaired by eshyra-uiax (B5); this bead normalizes the contract
shape, it does not re-own that repair. The implemented rows of
ENGINE_PROCEDURE_COVERAGE - restated as positive deterministic-capability
bindings by the W14 split - are the input set for the rest.

BOUNDED MEANING OF engine:F1-engine:F10 (design section 5.5)
engine:F1-F10 is the GENERATED MAGIC-ITEM CAPABILITY BACKLOG: 240 magic-item
records carrying executionReadiness, 1,016 clauses, 795 clauses declaring engine
hooks. No other record kind carries executionReadiness. It is not a corpus-wide
engine inventory, and this bead does not make it one. A green clause may still
declare an engine hook (magic-item:candle-of-invocation/c1-burn-time), so "green"
is not interchangeable with "hook-free", and neither the 794 engine-pending count
nor the 795 hook-carrying count may be reported as a capability inventory.

NON-GOALS AND PROHIBITIONS
- No corpus-wide capability inventory, and no claim of corpus-wide capability
  completeness.
- No widening of engine:F1-F10 beyond the generated magic-item backlog.
- No global deterministic-closure claim, and no revival of the withdrawn
  zero-engine-pending bar.
- Absence of a capability binding is a statement about Eshyra, not about the
  rules: it means only that no deterministic capability was positively selected.
  It never means the record has no mechanics, the rule is irrelevant, or the pack
  is complete. "Unbound", "unclassified", and "not recognized" are not safety
  properties.
- A deterministic operation does not imply a complete record: one clause of a
  record may be a positively executable capability while another has no engine
  owner (magic-item:ammunition-1-2-or-3 exhibits exactly that).
- No capability may be inferred from the presence of typed fields.
- Taxonomy hazard preserved: engine:F1-F10, the CLOSED epic eshyra-2n1t's
  different F1-F10, and the fable:F1-F8 findings are unrelated namespaces.

DEPENDENCIES
eshyra-uiax (B5, fail-closed repair on the pilot contract) and the approved
ENGINE_PROCEDURE_COVERAGE split owned by W14 (design section 5.4 part 2, the
positive deterministic-capability bindings). Contract-shape design is
parallel-safe; applying it to the split rows is not.

PERMANENT EVIDENCE
For each capability in force, an in-band declaration of the five fields and a
test that feeds unrecognized input and asserts the failure; an assertion that no
capability is derived from typed-field presence; an in-band statement of the
bounded meaning of engine:F1-F10 wherever the families are reported.

REQUIRED NEXT STATE
Every positively selected capability declares operation, inputs, exclusions,
revision/identity, and residual interpretation, and fails closed on unrecognized
input. The eshyra-olc5 capability families are reassessed against the bounded
magic-item scope rather than deleted: the underlying magic-item obligations
remain real.

MATERIAL CHANGE: yes. It defines the capability-contract shape that ADR 0020
section 3 requires.
acceptance_criteria:
Every deterministic capability in force declares, in band, its operation, its
required inputs, its exclusions, its revision or identity, and the interpretation
that remains with the DM; each has a test that feeds an unrecognized or
malformed input and asserts fail-closed behavior rather than a skip or a pass.
assertMagicItemOperationReady (derived-magic-item-clauses-v1) is restated in that
shape once eshyra-uiax has repaired its unrecognized-scope fail-open, and the
implemented rows produced by the W14 ENGINE_PROCEDURE_COVERAGE split are restated
in the same shape. No capability is inferred from the presence of typed pack
fields. Every report of engine:F1-engine:F10 states in band that the families are
the generated magic-item capability backlog (240 magic-item records with
executionReadiness, 1,016 clauses, 795 declaring engine hooks) and not a
corpus-wide engine inventory; no readiness or engine-hook count is presented as a
capability inventory, and a green clause carrying an engine hook is handled
correctly. Nothing in this work claims corpus-wide capability completeness,
global deterministic closure, or that an absent capability binding says anything
about the rules; absence is reported only as "no deterministic capability
positively selected". The engine:F* / eshyra-2n1t F* / fable:F* namespace
distinction is preserved wherever the families are named.

design accepted as the deliverable of eshyra-o9bd.19.8 (PR #485, reviewed head
afd113c7090378c3a9f4122f246a6c32602a5164, merge commit
042ce119aa699f04f60a1885d471335f07745282). They are parented to the ACTIVE
transition epic (eshyra-o9bd.19, or eshyra-olc5 for W13) rather than to the
closed design bead, so lifecycle semantics stay honest; eshyra-o9bd.19.8 remains
the design authority and is referenced from each description.

BOUNDARY THAT MUST NOT ERODE (design sections 8.4 and 14.3): campaign-rule
persistence and ruling lifecycle do not move out of eshyra-jhpt under any of
these items. W11 consumes; it does not own. If the jhpt interface proves
insufficient, the correct response is an amendment or a child under eshyra-jhpt,
never a discovery-local store.
